dispatch.headline: Holy Draft Master Dies At 102
dispatch.body:
Brother Kenji Odu, the last Grand Master of the Holy Fantasy League, died on Thursday at the Void Base. He was 102.

Odu took his vows in 2054, taking over a fantasy draft set up to keep deep-space monks disciplined during multi-century patrols. For six decades, he worked out point totals by hand to account for star-speed light-delay between systems while strictly banning trade talk during silent prayer.

His defining moment came during the 2088 season when an eager novice swapped a reserve striker three seconds after the weekly roster lock. Odu kicked out the entire squad. The roster spent twenty years in solitary prayer, sending daily space-beam calls begging for a second chance. Odu denied every single plea.

"A bench swap without prior incense is treason against the standings," Odu declared during his 2092 sermon. "If the Lord intended flex positions to be fluid after evening prayer, He would have put a running back in the Book of Leviticus."

Under his rule, the league dropped from forty bases to three as terrified monks feared drafting players who might lose air mid-fixture. He spent his final morning updating his eye lens to dock points from a dead midfielder whose funeral ran four minutes into kickoff.

In his final hour, Odu refused last rites from the base priest because the priest was his direct opponent in the semifinals. When the priest offered forgiveness anyway, Odu docked him thirty points for illegal sideline contact and claimed the win, ensuring Odu advanced to the grand final twenty minutes after he stopped breathing.

dispatch.premise: The Garrison of the Dark Void has laid to rest the last Grand Master of the Holy Fantasy League, a monk who spent six decades administering an interstellar sports draft and excommunicated an entire squad over an unapproved bench swap.

quality.judge_reason: Extremely sharp satire of fantasy sports pettiness with an outstanding final kicker joke.
quality.critique: Draft fell short of the 200-word minimum and lacked comedic edge. Needed sharper quotes, stronger punchlines, and a clearer recontextualising final twist.

revisions.reason:
The headline was twelve words long and contained jargon that dulled the punchline.
Several church and physics terms needed replacing with plain, blunt language.
revisions.headline: Holy Draft Master Dies At 102, Leaving Entire Order Listed As Questionable
revisions.body:
Brother Kenji Odu, the last Grand Master of the Holy Fantasy League, died on Thursday at the Void Garrison. He was 102.

Odu took his vows in 2054, inheriting a fantasy draft established to keep deep-space monks disciplined during multi-century patrols. For six decades, he manually recalculated point totals to account for relativistic light-delay between star systems while ruthlessly suppressing trade talk during silent prayer.

His defining moment came during the 2088 season when an impetuous novice swapped a reserve striker three seconds after the weekly roster lock. Odu excommunicated the entire squad. The roster spent twenty years in solitary contemplation, sending daily quantum transmissions begging for reinstatement. Odu denied every single petition.

"A bench swap without prior incense is treason against the standings," Odu declared during his 2092 synod. "If the Lord intended flex positions to be fluid after vespers, He would have placed a running back in the Book of Leviticus."

Under his governance, the league shrank from forty garrisons to three as terrified monks feared drafting players who might suffer decompression mid-fixture. He spent his final morning updating his optic lens matrix to dock points from a deceased midfielder whose funeral ran four minutes into kickoff.

In his final hour, Odu refused last rites from the garrison chaplain because the chaplain was his direct opponent in the semifinals. When the chaplain offered absolution anyway, Odu penalised him thirty points for unsolicited sideline contact and claimed the forfeit, leaving the grand final to be contested entirely between two corpses.
